title: Slain family man cherished kids
article: Robert Scott Carpenter -- a talented musician who composed and sang a song for each of his three sisters as a gift for their weddings -- was remembered as a loving father and devoted husband by more than 200 mourners who attended his funeral Thursday.

Carpenter was fatally shot at his 258 McCurdy Dr. home by an Amherstburg police officer shortly after 7 a.m. Monday. The province's Special Investigations Unit continues to investigate and is expected to issue a report in two weeks.

The service at Amherstburg's James H. Sutton funeral home began with an acoustic version of the Rolling Stone's anthem, You Can't Always Get What You Want. The song was played by Curtis Muldoon, a long-time friend of Carpenter's.

The pair played together for about 10 years in the band Nightbreed. Carpenter, a former teacher at Leone's Music World, sang and played guitar for the rock group but had given it up about five years ago to focus on his family.
With his common-law wife, Lisa Stewart, Carpenter, 37, had two children, Sarah, 3 and Noah, 2. He also had a son, Kyle, 12, who lives with his mother in Barrie.
A devastated Stewart, who was home at the time of the shooting, fought through tears Thursday as she read a poem she wrote for her companion of five years entitled "I Am."

Carpenter's three sisters -- Shelley, Stacey and Sherry -- stood closely together as they spoke briefly but lovingly about their only brother. They remembered him for his love of animals and motorycles and talked about his desire to learn more about computers. But most of all they remembered him as a devoted father who loved music but cherished his children even more. Donations may be made in trust to Sarah and Noah.
"This is a tragedy that happened, a sad tragedy," said Rev. Maynard Hurst."In this community, blessedly, it's not something that occurs often."
